notes: The picture is now very clear and it changes the recommendation completely. Report 1 shows Marrowby & Vane gets 51.6% of shipments from Albion Parcel — the exact carrier the COO team flagged as broken from November onward — while Report 2 shows Marrowby & Vane's delivery-tagged tickets were near-normal all year (240-1,196 min/ticket, Feb-Oct) until November (9,533 min, 61.8% breach) and December (19,274 min, 100% breach). That's a live, ongoing carrier failure, not a staffing gap. Studio Vrij tells a different story: its delivery-ticket resolution time exploded in May-July 2025 (8,528 / 29,549 / 8,763 minutes) and then fully recovered by September-December (83-680 minutes, 0% breach) — this matches almost exactly what the VP Customer Experience team posted last week about a merchant's 'local May 2025 delivery breakdown... not a platform-wide issue.' That was very likely Studio Vrij, and it's already over. Neither merchant looks like a 'hire more agents' case. Tonight I want to (1) pin the Albion Parcel collapse specifically to Marrowby & Vane's own shipments month-by-month to nail the mechanism and check if it's still ongoing, (2) find which of Studio Vrij's carriers caused the May-July spike and confirm it's genuinely resolved, and (3) run the clean controlled comparison Mia actually needs for a decision: strip the known incident months out of each tenant's numbers and see if what's left still looks worse than Cragsley's baseline, or whether the whole gap was the carrier event. On the knowledge-base question: the event_name inventory (Report 3) shows only 8 tracked events platform-wide — none related to viewing a help/KB article — so combined with last week's zero-match page_views test, I'm closing that question as 'not measurable with current instrumentation' rather than spending another slot guessing.
